verdict.line: You lose the laning phase to kiting and solo-kill pressure before level 6, but the matchup is a measured 55% win rate because Fury of the Sands and stacked Siphoning Strike flip it late.

brief.thesis: Gnar's ranged Q (Boomerang Throw) and E (Hop) bounce give Mini Gnar a kiting shell that wins trades and solo kills before you have tools to close distance. Nasus has no way to answer that range until R (Fury of the Sands) comes online at 6, after which stacked Q and Wither let you force fights on your terms instead of his.

theirWindow.when: Mini Gnar, Rage bar near max
theirWindow.what: He's about to transform into Mega Gnar, trading his long-range Boomerang Throw and Hop bounce for a point-blank Wallop stun and an AoE Crunch landing. Don't walk up for a trade right as the bar fills, the damage profile flips instantly.

yourWindow.when: R (Fury of the Sands) is up, post-6
yourWindow.what: Go in. The bonus Health, Attack Range, and cast range from R let you stick to his kite pattern that normally wins the exchange, and the Max Health drain punishes any extended fight.

powerCurve.note: Boomerang Throw range outpokes your melee Q
R and Wither let you start sticking
Q stacks and Trinity Force close the gap
Full build and R uptime overwhelm his kite

start.why: 56.4% win rate over 140 games as the top start. The sustain and poke reduction matter against a lane where Boomerang Throw and autos are chipping you down before you can trade back.

boots.why: 52.4% win rate over 63 games, the stronger of the two boot options here. Gnar's damage is almost entirely physical autos and Boomerang Throw hits, so the flat auto-attack reduction outvalues the haste from Ionian Boots in this specific matchup.

core.why: Leads the highest win-rate path (58.3% over 12 games) and gives you the move speed and damage spike needed to stop getting kited once R is online.
Second item on both top-performing paths. The attack speed slow helps you actually land stacks on a kiting target, and the armor covers his auto-reliant damage.
Closes out the top path at 58.3% win rate. Stacks your Soul Eater lifesteal and R's health drain into sustained healing through extended fights.

situational.when: you need the slow online earlier to catch his transform windows (85.7% win rate over 7 games on this path, small sample)
the enemy team is building around sustained auto-attack damage rather than burst (62.5% win rate on this alternate path)
you're still getting kited in the midgame and need raw move speed to close gaps

runes.keystoneWhy: Top performing page at 55.4% win rate. The healing and move speed burst offset Gnar's poke damage during the levels 1-5 window where you can't fight back, and it's the only keystone here that doesn't require you to already be winning trades.

summoners.why: Flash+Ghost posts the highest win rate of the three measured combos (62% over a 26.3% pick rate). Ghost closes the range gap on a kiting Mini Gnar during farm phases, and Flash answers Mega Gnar's Wallop stun or an R (GNAR!) knockback into a wall.

playing.title: Farm from max range early
playing.detail: Stay at the edge of his 1100-range Boomerang Throw through levels 1-5. Don't step into melee range to stack Siphoning Strike until Wither is off cooldown to slow him first.

playing.title: Track the Rage Gene bar constantly
playing.detail: At max Rage his next ability turns him into Mega Gnar, swapping his kiting Q and bouncing E for a close-range Wallop stun and an AoE Crunch landing. Reposition before that bar fills, not after.

playing.title: Open trades with Wither, not Q
playing.detail: Cast W (Wither, 700 range) to decelerate his Movement and Attack Speed before closing into your 255-range Siphoning Strike. Going in Q-first just lets him kite you at full speed.

playing.title: Save all-ins for R availability
playing.detail: Fury of the Sands (120s cooldown) gives you bonus Health, Attack Range, and cast range plus Max Health drain on nearby enemies. Don't force extended fights before 6 or before R is off cooldown.

playing.title: Punish his Boomerang Throw cooldown
playing.detail: Early ranks on Q are 16/14.5/13s unless he catches the boomerang. When it's down and uncaught, that's your window to shove the wave or step up safely for a stack.

playing.title: Shred with Spirit Fire on full waves
playing.detail: E (Spirit Fire, 650 range, 12s cooldown flat) reduces Armor on anyone standing in it. Use it on cannon waves to snowball your Siphoning Strike stack growth faster.

playing.title: Respect Mega Gnar's Crunch landing
playing.detail: Unlike Mini Gnar's bouncing Hop, Mega Gnar's E deals area damage on landing with no bounce. Don't facecheck a trade right as his Rage bar approaches max.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, boots, runes, and summoner spells above are pulled directly from OP.GG's measured games on the current patch (16.20.1); the win rates and sample sizes are real. The lane-by-lane tactical reading, timing windows, and ability interactions are my own analysis layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Keep some distance to avoid being kited by Mini Gnar while you farm. Keep your [Q] stacks up and wait for an opportunity to go in post-level 6.
